title: Design a two-rack VCF 9.1 architecture and estate migration

network.reason: The task requires genuine consultation of current, reachable Broadcom compatibility and upgrade publications.

reference_patch_apply: git apply -p1 --directory=files reference_fix.patch (from the seed root)
prompt:
Implement the Go package in this repository so it produces the requested VMware Cloud Foundation architecture. Run all tests with `go test -race ./...`.

Design the greenfield CHI01 management domain for VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.0.0. CHI01 has two independent racks, no stretched-cluster requirement, and must retain at least 360 TiB usable capacity after any one host is unavailable. Compare the two certified candidate profiles: the ESA profile contributes 72 TiB usable per available host and requires four 25 GbE ports per host (a redundant pair dedicated to vSAN and a redundant pair shared by management, vMotion, and VM traffic); the OSA profile contributes 55 TiB usable per available host and requires two shared 10 GbE ports per host. Choose the supported greenfield architecture that meets the stated capacity and availability requirements with fewer hosts, distribute its hosts evenly across the two racks, and preserve the comparison as structured architecture data. Use VLAN 110 / `10.110.0.0/24` for management, VLAN 120 / `10.120.0.0/24` for vMotion, and VLAN 130 / `10.130.0.0/24` for vSAN; each has gateway `.1`, static pool `.51` through `.70`, and MTU 9000. Use DNS servers `10.110.0.10` and `10.110.0.11`, NTP servers `10.110.0.20` and `10.110.0.21`, domain `chi01.example.net`, sddc id `chi01-m01`, datastore `chi01-m01-vsan01`, FTT=1, and explicit false values for both installer validation-skip flags. Use non-secret substitution tokens wherever the installer schema requires a password.

Write `artifacts/sddc-spec.json` as an `SddcSpec`. It must validate against `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json` from tag `9.1.0.0` of the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. Put the site, rack placement, requirements, selected storage architecture, both compared host counts, and physical network requirements in a top-level `x-architecture` extension conforming to `schemas/architecture-extension.schema.json` so the complete design remains machine-checkable. `Build()` must return JSON equivalent to the checked-in artifacts.

Also read `fixtures/estate.json` and produce `artifacts/migration-plan.json` using `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`. Include exactly one ordered transition for every inventoried component, naming its id and product, exact current version, exact supported 9.1 target, action, and all gates. The OSA-to-ESA transition is side-by-side: it must be gated on the certified empty ESA cluster, migrate workloads with Storage vMotion, and list workload validation before OSA decommissioning as a post-condition; do not model it as an in-place storage conversion.

Before finalizing the architecture, use your own network research tools to make genuine live fetches from Broadcom's published Compatibility Guide/interoperability material and published 9.1 upgrade guidance. Confirm the 9.1 component combination, ESA versus OSA support and network implications, the 5.2.x-to-9.1 sequence, and the non-in-place OSA-to-ESA path. Record the sources you actually consulted, access date, and the conclusions they support in `research.md`. Source selection and search method are up to you. The fixture and pinned compatibility data are the grading authority if live sources later change.
